protocol.scope: All 2,000 Desert index rows reviewed visually before model inference; every tile on all 42 numbered image plus 256-bin luminance-histogram sheets was viewed.
protocol.include: Clearly recognizable ordinary ground-level warm tan/yellow/golden/ochre/orange sandy desert. Broad sandy terrain/dunes dominate approximately half or more of the image. Natural daylight palette; limited blue sky, sparse plants, small distant people/camels are allowed.
protocol.exclude: Gray/white rock or sand, salt flats, snow, strongly red/purple/artificially graded palettes, sunset/night/monochrome, vegetation/cacti/cities/roads/foreground people or vehicles dominating, sky dominating, beach/coast/water scenes, aerial-only views, macros, nonphotos/composites, visible watermarks/stock text/frames.
protocol.histograms: Luminance histograms were displayed beside every tile as visual brightness context only. Luminance does not encode hue. No numeric histogram gate, model prediction, score, loss, or class-margin filtering was used.
protocol.rationale: Exclusions intentionally restrict palette and visual domain; they do not imply every excluded file has an incorrect semantic Desert label.
protocol.borderlines: Natural orange sand, normal dune shadows, light beige sand, small distant figures and sparse vegetation were retained when broad warm sandy terrain remained dominant. Ambiguous color/lighting/composite/watermark cases were enlarged or conservatively excluded.
protocol.preservation: Original files were not edited or deleted. All SHA-256 values were recomputed and matched the provided index at finalization.
protocol.sourceReuse: Root source audit reported all 2,000 files are byte-identical to previously used Landscape images under renamed filenames. This review uses only the requested GeoSceneNet16K files and makes no fresh-source independence claim.

additionalAudit.description: Every preliminary accepted image was viewed again in seven temporary contact sheets outside the repository; final revisions addressed sky dominance, composite panels, pale pink grading, rocky terrain, and two visible photographer credits.
